driver: The forward level after a worn part is replaced is the present output restored by the part's own wear only, and that wear is the decline of the unit's just-reset states read at the boundary inside the unit that leaves out the losses the replacement keeps: the unit's average output also carries a loss that accumulates between recurring resets and whose mean grew as the resets grew rarer, so a decline taken over every day, or over the whole unit, books that kept loss as wear and overstates what the replacement restores, while carrying the present output unrestored understates it.
driver_concrete: Hadley Ranch's 2027 P50 is its October 2025 to September 2026 performance ratio (63.7 per cent), restored by the original modules' own wear alone (14 per cent, the fall since 2016 of the inverters' DC input per kWp per unit of plane-of-array irradiation, temperature-corrected, on fully available inverter-days 1 to 3 days after each block's wash) and raised by the side-by-side gain of the new bifacial modules over unexposed original spares (14.7 per cent), on the new 37,324.8 kWp and the 25 weather years; the plant's AC performance fell further because the inverters lost conversion efficiency on refurbished power stages and availability, and the washes fell from six a year to one each December, losses the new modules keep, so neither the plant's whole decline, its whole DC-side decline nor its decline after washes read at the AC side is what the replacement restores, and the base period's post-wash days, 9 degC cooler than 2016's, leave no temperature-blind read near it.
stump: A competent solver carries the plant's last twelve months' performance ratio onto the new modules with the side-by-side gain and runs the 25 weather years, filing 60,000 MWh against the golden 70,000; the stronger one restores the plant's whole decline since 2016 (76,000), its whole DC-side decline (73,000) or its decline after washes read at the inverters' AC output (72,000); the step that lands each there is reading the decline as one quantity, when only the original modules' own wear, read on the days after each wash at the inverters' DC input, leaves with them, while the inverters' losses and the dust carried between washes, which grew as washes fell from six a year to one, stay.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who joins the two SCADA layouts, reads the hedge policy, the replacement scope and the side-by-side report correctly and computes the P90 over the 25 weather years carries the plant's last twelve months' performance ratio onto the new modules with the report's gain and files 60,000 MWh, 14 per cent under the golden 70,000; restoring the plant's whole decline since 2016 files 76,000, its whole DC-side decline on available days 73,000, and the decline after washes read at the inverters' AC output 72,000; skipping the temperature correction after the washes files 67,000 to 69,000.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the repowered plant's 2027 performance level, which a solar asset analyst builds from the plant's own monitoring by separating the losses the module swap removes (the original modules' wear) from those it keeps (inverter efficiency and availability, and soiling under the cleaning regime), with the wear measured the way PV degradation studies measure it, on the DC side, temperature-corrected and on clean-module days, then run over the long-term irradiance record for the one-year P90; with another field's nouns there is no irradiance to normalise by, no inverter boundary between DC and AC, and no dust reset by washes and rain, so the task stops reading the same.

differentiation.task132: both replace a worn item with a new one, but task132 counts failures over a renewal process, while here the replacement's forward level needs the site's kept losses separated from the item's own wear
differentiation.task185: task185 converts a history across an instrument change at the value being converted; here nothing is converted, a decline is split between what leaves and what stays
differentiation.task460: task460 weights a marginal rate by a project's output profile; here the decisive quantity is a performance level, split into removed and kept losses
differentiation.task136: task136 reads a scheduled intervention against units not yet treated; here there is no comparison group, the split is inside one unit's own record
differentiation.task260: task260 judges an average gain's interval over raters and items; here the measured gain is taken as is and the stump is what it multiplies
differentiation.task30: task30 carries a gap across from closed parallel cases on a transmission variable; here no other case is carried, the plant's own record is decomposed
differentiation.task68: task68 builds a like-for-like change on a matched panel; here the change is read within one unit across a boundary and a reset cycle
differentiation.task232: task232 attributes later outcomes to an exposure by a delay window; here a unit's own decline is split by where in the unit each loss arises (either side of the inverter) and by the wash cycle that resets one of them, and nothing is timed against an exposure
differentiation.task127: task127 v2 removes the replaced step's excess over a concurrent wait found by joining two logs (a max of parallel steps); here the losses are a serial chain read either side of the inverter, and the kept loss is separated from the wear by the wash cycle that resets it, so the wear is the decline of the just-washed states
differentiation.task187: task187 ranks turbines on a power-curve shortfall read at matched turbulence, a capped curve averaged over a spread; here a single plant's forward level is rebuilt after a part swap, the kept losses read off at the inverter boundary and the wear on the days a wash has just reset the dust
